newsitem.title: USA: Ekco closing Massachusetts, Ohio plants.
newsitem.headline: Ekco closing Massachusetts, Ohio plants.

text.p: The Ekco Group Inc said it will close cleaning products manufacturing plants in Massachusetts and Ohio and move 200 jobs to Mexico in an effort to lower costs.

The shift, to be completed over 18 months, resulted in the housewares manufacturer and marketer taking a pre-tax charge of $6.5 million for the fourth quarter related to severance costs and the writing down of assets.
The Nashua, N.H. company's stock closed at $4 off 3/4 of a point. Ekco products include: bakeware, kitchenware, plastic storage bins, brooms, brushes and mops.
Ekco said it expects revenues and net income for the third quarter to be lower than analysts' expectations and prior year results.
The Easthampton, Massachusetts plant employs 220 people in three shifts and makes househouse brushes. The Hamilton, Ohio plat employs 70 people and makes long-handled brooms and mops.
Ekco Vice President and Treasurer John Haran said the company will expand production at a kitchenwares plant it already operates in Obregon.

The company said it expects revenues for the quarter ending September 29 to be about $80 million and net income to be about $2 million, or 10 cents a share, before the effect of certain special charges. Ecko expects to announce actual results for the quarter during the week of October 21. The company anticipates losses of $22 million, or $1.53 a share for the fiscal year.
